name: Rotterdam The Hague Airport
before:
One airport for Rotterdam and The Hague, 5.5 km north north west of Rotterdam, and third busiest in the Netherlands with over 2.1 million passengers in 2019. It flies to European city and leisure destinations.

Getting into either city is simple. Bus line 33 runs from Rotterdam Centraal through the airport to Meijersplein station, where metro line E connects frequently to Den Haag Centraal, Rotterdam Centraal and the city centre. The A13 motorway runs alongside.

It is also a busy general aviation field, with flying clubs, a skydiving club and a flight training school based here.

The airport exists because of the war. Rotterdam's original airport at Waalhaven was wrecked in the German bombing of the city and then destroyed outright to stop the Germans using it, so a new site was found in the Zestienhoven polder, which gave the airport its old name. It opened in October 1956.

KLM Cityhopper's Heathrow route, the longest running service here, was dropped in 2008.
after:
One airport for Rotterdam and The Hague, 5.5 km north north west of Rotterdam, and the third busiest in the Netherlands with about 2.4 million passengers in 2025. It flies to more than 50 destinations, most of them European city and holiday destinations.

Getting into either city is simple. Bus 33 runs from Rotterdam Centraal to the airport and on to Meijersplein station, where metro line E connects to Den Haag Centraal and Rotterdam Centraal.

It is also a busy general aviation field, with a flying club and flight school based here.

Rotterdam's pre-war airport at Waalhaven was destroyed in the Second World War, so a new site was found in the Zestienhoven polder. The new airport opened in 1956.

Transavia has a base here, and British Airways flies to London City.

claims.claim: busy general aviation field with a flying club and flight school
claims.inAfter: It is also a busy general aviation field, with a flying club and flight school based here.
claims.note: Was "flying clubs, a skydiving club and a flight training school". The operator's 2025 figures bear out "busy": 37,299 of its 58,654 aircraft movements in 2025 were light aircraft under 6 tonnes, and 17,687 were training flights. Its own news (19 September 2026) confirms the Rotterdamsche Aero Club, a flying club and flight school, is based here. The skydiving club has only Wikipedia.
